fresh_visual_facts: The candidate's book-title captions outside and directly below the cover rectangles have visibly contrasting thick/thin strokes and serif/Song-style terminals. They appear substantially heavier than the original reference's external title captions.

The matching original reference's external title captions have a medium-weight sans appearance, with more uniform strokes and no visible Song-style terminals. Shared titles such as the moon, summer-observatory and sleepless-city books support the comparison even though the filtered order differs.
Only the outer captions are compared. Typography printed inside cover artwork is treated as source art and is not used as evidence for UI-caption family or weight.
At the provided original view, the external captions are legible. Exact runtime font file/family and numeric runtime weight cannot be established from PNG appearance alone.

observations.topic: Paperwhite update toast placement and fine-note constraints
fresh_visual_facts: The toast is a centered white rectangle with a black border and black text, approximately x=219..400,y=635..684 in the native 618 x 824 capture.

It overlaps the lower portions of the second-row middle cover rectangles and their outer caption strip. The right part of the night-garden title is hidden and the silver-mountain outer title region is behind the toast; the left and right book captions outside its horizontal span remain visible.

The folio 1/6 and right Next action remain visible below the toast. The dock beginning near y=752, its icons/labels and selected Library marker are fully visible. The page outside the toast is not dimmed.
The message reports that demo mode did not check updates, rather than claiming that a provider update check completed.

The authorized foundation crop literally labels the toast pattern as no occlusion and no dimming, and its fine note specifies a white background/black border/black text, disappearance after two seconds, and refresh limited to the toast rectangle.
A single PNG does not establish click interception, modal/input blocking, two-second disappearance, or rectangle-only refresh. Those interaction and timing semantics are left to Root.
